page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Top left: page number 150. Top centre: running head DIALECTICAE. Main text in one column, a chapter heading centred mid-page, then the woodcut-initialed paragraph. Bottom right: catchword "liquid".

main_text.l: causa est. Cæsar vicit Pompeium: Cæsar fuit
victor Pompeij.
Quid igitur de iis quæ de futuro aliquid
dicunt, deque eo quod possit fieri, aut non pos-
sit: de quibus Cicero in libro de Fato quæstio-
nem logicæ artis obscurissimam esse scribit?
Sanè disputari posset, non verè & proprie illas
Enuntiationes esse. primùm quia non sunt ha-
bitus: deinde quia Medij, quod est quasi nor-
ma diiudicandæ conuenientiæ inter subiectũ
& attributum, de quo in Argumentationibus
intelliges: adhiberi ad ea quæ non sunt, non
potest. Sed quoniam rerũ naturalium certus
quidam ordo est à Deo constitutus, cuius pro-
pterea certus videtur euétus, vt in Solis & Lu-
næ defectionibus, quarum causæ naturales
sunt: propterea fatius est, illas Philosophorum
argutias non attingere,
Diuisio Enuntiationum. CAP. X.
VOTVPLEX[?] est Enuntiatio? Du-
plex. Vna quæ est simplex, quâ Græci ti[?] κατηγορικῶ[?] vocant: altera copula-
ta, quâ iidem συνθετικῶ[?] appellant.
Quæ est Simplex? Quæ de uno tantùm, id-
que purè & absolutè vel affirmat, vel negat. vt
Iuti, Mors est horribilis, mors non est horribi-
lis, Filius heres esto. Filius exheres esto.
Quæ est prima diuisio simplicis Enuntia-
tionis? Vt alia sit affirmatiua, quæ vnum a-
liquid

page.notes: Long s (s) normalised to plain s throughout, so "caussa" appears as "causa" and "est" as "est". Printed "caussa" with double s may be a 16th/17th-century spelling; the form on the scan is uncertain. Woodcut initial at the start of the Enuntiatio paragraph: first letter uncertain, transcribed as V[?]. Greek in the Græci sentence is only partly legible: "ti" at the start of the line after "Græ-" is uncertain, and the Greek words κατηγορικῶ and συνθετικῶ are my best reading and are marked [?]. "Iuti" is printed as shown; the reading is uncertain. The catchword "liquid" is the last line on the page, set at the right, and is not repeated in the text.
